newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N. commissioner for refugees to visit S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: U.N. commissioner for refugees to visit S.Africa.

text.p: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees, Sadako Ogata, will pay an official visit to South Africa next week to brief political leaders on the continent's refugee crises, the UNHCR said on Saturday.

Ogata kicks off her four-day stay by meeting President Nelson Mandela in Cape Town on Monday. She would hold talks with the leader of the country's largest black opposition, Inkatha's Mangosuthu Buthelezi, on Tuesday.
"The purpose of her visit is to brief South African leaders on Africa's refugee crises and the urgent need for solutions," the UNHCR office in Pretoria said in a statement.
The UNHCR estimates there are 5.6 million refugees in Africa. Key flashpoints are the Great Lakes region and Angola.
Mandela has launched a bid to help broker a truce in Zaire between rebel leader Laurent Kabila and President Mobutu Sese Seko's government.
